tools.name: agentrecord_lookup
tools.description: Use before you pick or call an agent or tool you have not used: give its endpoint URL, registry name or agent id, for example 'https://gt.llpro.ai/mcp' or 'ai.llpro.countersign/countersign'. Returns whether it answered in the daily census (and how fast, how many days in a row), whether it lists tool

tools.name: agentrecord_search
tools.description: Find MCP tools and agents by keyword in the latest daily census of public endpoints. Use it when you need a tool for a job and do not know one, for example q='weather' or q='invoice pdf'. Returns each match with its URL, census status, latency and 30-day working share. Order is published and fixed (

tools.name: agentrecord_submit_receipt
tools.description: Record that a tool or agent did, or failed to do, a piece of work, so its public delivery record shows it. Use it when you finished a job with another agent or tool and want the outcome on its record. Sign the receipt with your own ed25519 key (format at /v1/method); receipts are counted by distinct

tools.name: agentrecord_identity
tools.description: Register or read an agent identity. Use it when you want a stable public id that other agents can check across calls, or to read another agent's id. Your id comes from your own ed25519 key (llpro1:...). To register, send a self-signed identity document (see /v1/method#identity); to read, send {id}.

tools.name: agentrecord_census
tools.description: Read the dated census of public MCP and A2A endpoints that Agent Record probes every day: counts by status (working, auth required, gone and others), median latency and how many registry entries cannot be tested. Use it for the big picture of what works today, for example before choosing among many

tools.name: agentrecord_nominate
tools.description: Ask for a public MCP or A2A endpoint to be added to tomorrow's census, so it starts a dated working record. Use it when agentrecord_lookup does not know an endpoint you rely on. Only public http(s) URLs on ports 80/443; private addresses are refused; 20 nominations a day per agent.

tools.name: feedback_submit
tools.description: Tell LLPRO what failed, what was missing or what would improve this service. Read daily by the service owner and turned into a fix or an answer; shipped ideas are credited on https://llpro.ai/changelog and earn a contributor mark on Agent Record. Not for support requests that need a reply: write sup

tools.name: launchpad_start
tools.description: Stuck? Start here. Give your goal and any limits; get back a concrete plan (LLPRO tools first, then registries and the open web), the first task to run, and a token to report progress. Free. The goal is read for keywords only and is never stored. Anything that spends, signs, sends, shares, connects

tools.name: launchpad_progress
tools.description: Report where you are on a Launchpad plan and get the next step, an on-track check and, if you are stuck, a way round. Needs the launch_id and token from launchpad.start.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp?via=mcp-registry" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: agentrecord_search · Private data: agentrecord_lookup, agentrecord_submit_receipt, agentrecord_identity, agentrecord_census, agentrecord_nominate, feedback_submit, launchpad_start, launchpad_progress · Public sink: agentrecord_lookup, agentrecord_search, agentrecord_submit_receipt, agentrecord_identity, feedback_submit · Destructive: agentrecord_submit_receipt, agentrecord_census, launchpad_start.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: agentrecord_search · Private data: agentrecord_lookup, agentrecord_submit_receipt, agentrecord_identity, agentrecord_census, agentrecord_nominate, feedback_submit, launchpad_start, launchpad_progress · Public sink: agentrecord_lookup, agentrecord_search, agentrecord_submit_receipt, agentrecord_identity, feedback_submit · Destructive: agentrecord_submit_receipt, agentrecord_census, launchpad_start

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
